problem: Existing VLN benchmarks are embodiment-agnostic, evaluate against a single ground-truth path, and ignore that real navigation depends on the agent's mobility (e.g. stairs, narrow passages, elevators). VLMs used as navigation planners therefore may propose routes that are infeasible or unsafe for a given agent.
motivation: VLMs are increasingly used as navigation assistants for robots and assistive systems, where many plausible routes exist and validity depends on the agent's physical size and abilities. A benchmark with per-edge, per-agent traversability labels is needed to measure this capability-conditioned reasoning and diagnose failures.
key_idea: Benchmark capability-conditioned navigation: given a tour video, a node list, an agent profile (human, wheelchair, sweeper, humanoid, quadruped) and an A-to-B task, a VLM must predict feasibility, a valid node path and a reason, scored against edge-level traversability ground truth.
insight: Performance drops as constraints tighten (mean CapNav 57.83% for the unconstrained human vs 39.12% for the humanoid). Models handle visually salient obstacles (stairs, door sills) far better than obstacles needing metric estimation (narrow clearance, turning space), i.e. 'dimension neglect'. More frames or thinking help unevenly (thinking +6.87 CapNav on average at about 8x latency; frame gains are larger for stronger models), indicating a cross-frame visual integration bottleneck. A pilot LoRA fine-tune raises the score but lowers reasoning validity and adds false positives on narrow passages.
method: Task formulation: each query is a Space–Task–Capability triple (tour video + node list, source-to-target instruction, agent profile JSON with footprint, vertical limits and manipulation abilities); the VLM outputs feasibility, a node path and a rationale.

Data construction: 45 scenes from HM3D/Matterport3D, 2 FPS tour videos rendered in Habitat at 1.5 m eye height and 75° FOV, hand-annotated navigation graphs (avg 13.8 nodes, 14.5 edges), tasks generated by Gemini 2.5 Pro and manually verified (2,365 QA pairs in total).

Ground truth: per-edge binary traversability for each agent, annotated by manually driving agent-sized colliders in a 3D annotation UI, with textual reasons for blocked edges. Task feasibility is defined as the existence of a simple path whose edges are all traversable (5,075 labels, 3,945 positive / 1,130 negative).

Metrics: Feas-F1 (feasibility), Path Validity (PV, valid simple path from source to target on the graph), Route Traversability Accuracy (RTA, fraction of traversable edges on the predicted path), Reasoning Validity (RV, LLM-as-judge with 89% agreement with humans on 300 samples). The composite CapNav score is the equal-weight average of the four.

Evaluation protocol: 13 VLMs tested in thinking and non-thinking modes, with 16/32/64 frames or 1 FPS (avg 163 frames); random-walk lower bound (29.35) and human reference (avg 60.59, range 49 to 75 on 20 tasks each).

Analysis tools: failure taxonomy (path hallucination, obstacle hallucination, dimension neglect, ability hallucination) mined by Gemini-3 and refined manually, obstacle-type breakdown, frame-budget study, and a pilot LoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-VL-8B on tasks augmented from 2K to 13K.

setting.backbone: 13 off-the-shelf VLMs (Gemini-2.5-pro/flash, GPT-5-pro, GPT-4.1, Doubao-Seed-1.6, Qwen3-VL-8B, InternVL3.5-8B/14B, Keye-VL-1.5-8B, MiMo-VL-7B, GLM-4.1V-9B, Spatial-MLLM-4B, Video-R1-7B), evaluated frozen, zero-shot
setting.model_size: benchmark; evaluated models range from 4B to proprietary
setting.training_data: none (benchmark, zero-shot evaluation); pilot LoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-VL-8B on 13K graph-augmented CapNav tasks
setting.observation: pre-recorded tour video (2 FPS, or 16/32/64 uniformly sampled frames, or 1 FPS) plus a textual node list and agent profile
setting.action_space: none (high-level output: feasibility yes/no, a node-sequence path on a navigation graph, and a text reason)
setting.simulator: Habitat (rendering videos from HM3D and Matterport3D scans)
setting.privileged: Global observation of the whole scene through the tour video and the annotated node list (passive setting); no ground-truth edges given at inference

numbers_note: Custom benchmark, not a canonical one; results are on the full set of 45 scenes with no official train/test split defined. Per-agent composite scores are also in Table 1 but only the aggregate metrics are listed here. Obstacle-type and frame-budget results are figures only.
results: All 13 VLMs beat the random walk (29.35), and the best proprietary models (Gemini-2.5-pro 67.18, GPT-5-pro 66.37) exceed the human average (60.59) but stay below the best human (74.77). Open-source models and the spatial-reasoning models Spatial-MLLM (30.15) and Video-R1 (37.39) trail far behind. Reasoning validity stays low for all models (best 47.89), and the humanoid embodiment is the hardest.
limitations: Passive setting with a pre-recorded video and a pre-annotated node graph; no interactive exploration, low-level control or real-robot evaluation.
Only five agent profiles and 45 scenes; the human reference comes from just four participants with 20 tasks each; RV depends on an LLM judge (89% agreement with humans).
Fine-tuning is only a pilot, and the paper offers no method that solves dimension neglect.
